title: icepack claw its way back to raleigh to face the bearcats
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Kaitlyn Alumbaugh/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C.  -   Following a quick road trip to Alabama that saw the Icepack go 1-1 in its two games there, N.C. State returns home to Lane Arena for its final set of home games before Winter Bre...
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C.  -   Following a quick road trip to Alabama that saw the Icepack go 1-1 in its two games there, N.C. State returns home to Lane Arena for its final set of home games before Winter Break against the Cincinnati Bearcats, with games scheduled for Thursday and Friday night.

The Bearcats enter this matchup with a 3-10-1 record, placing them last in the SECHL. Cincinnati also boasts a -46 goal differential, the second-worst mark in D1 ACHA, ahead of only Rochester Christian University. One of the main issues that’s plagued the Bearcats all season has been goaltending, as they have allowed 84 goals in 14 games, good for an average of six goals allowed per game. With Cincinnati struggling mightily on defense and in goal, the Bearcats will face a tough challenge against an Icepack team that has found its offensive rhythm.

The Icepack’s attack has been particularly dangerous during its recent stretch of games, scoring 26 goals in its last five contests, including an eight-goal performance in its win against Alabama last Friday night. Amid the offensive improvement, N.C. State has bounced back from its early-season struggles and climbed to third in the SECHL standings with 18 points in 16 games. Sitting just four points behind conference-leading Kentucky, the Icepack have the opportunity to gain even more ground with two favorable matchups against Cincinnati.

N.C. State forward Daniel Prazma has played a significant role in the Icepack’s recent offensive success, recording his second hat trick of the season during Friday’s win against Alabama. Prazma leads the Icepack with 24 points on the season, and has been a consistent offensive threat for the team throughout the year. Despite his individual success, Prazma believes much of the credit belongs to the team around him.

“The number one reason for my success can be credited to my teammates,” Prazma said. “Hockey is all about team play, so without my teammates finding me in the right areas and battling hard in the corners, not too many goals would come.”

Thursday and Friday’s games will mark the Icepack’s final appearances at Lane Arena until January 29, 2027. While N.C. State will undoubtedly welcome the extended break to rest and recover, the team is looking forward to putting on a show for the Icepack fanbase one last time before heading into the new year.

“I’m hoping for an awesome turnout this week,” Prazma said. “Cincinnati is going to be two great games that should be worth the watch, and I know me and all the boys thrive when playing in front of the awesome Icepack fanbase.”

title: Icepack split series with frozen tide in pelham
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Kaitlyn Alumbaugh/Icepack Hockey
summary: PELHAM, ALA.  -    Following its trip to Alabama, the Icepack split the weekend series against the Frozen Tide, winning Friday night 8-5, before dropping Saturday’s game 5-7.
paragraphs: PELHAM, ALA.  -    Following its trip to Alabama, the Icepack split the weekend series against the Frozen Tide, winning Friday night 8-5, before dropping Saturday’s game 5-7.

Friday’s contest saw the Icepack’s offense get to work early, as Daniel Prazma opened the scoring 3:19 into the first period, assisted by Jack Ammons. Prazma struck again minutes later to give N.C. State a 2-0 lead, assisted by Erik Dahlin and Nick Shook. All of the momentum seemed to belong to the Icepack early in the game. However, Alabama scored two goals within roughly three minutes of each other to tie the game midway through the period. Prazma completed his hat trick 15:16 into the first period, assisted by Dahlin and Mason Payne. Following a boarding penalty and game misconduct assessed to an Alabama player, Holden Koufman scored on the power play, assisted by Ammons and Andrew Throndson. The Icepack found itself on the penalty kill following a late high sticking penalty but maintained its 4-2 lead heading into the first intermission.

The second period began with a goal from the Frozen Tide less than a minute in on the power play. After allowing a goal on its first penalty kill, the Icepack was able to kill off the next penalty called against it minutes later. Koufman scored his second goal of the night midway through the second period, assisted by Ethan Hoover and Jack Napieralski. N.C. State killed off a cross checking penalty shortly after the goal, and no further goals or penalties followed the successful kill. Each team scored a goal in the period, meaning the Icepack headed into the third period with a 5-3 lead.

Both teams began the third period looking to establish control of the game, but an early slashing penalty against the Icepack led to a power play goal for the Frozen Tide less than 10 seconds later. N.C. State found itself on the kill again midway through the period, but Noah Fitzsimons gave the Icepack its momentum back with a shorthanded goal, assisted by Jake Lipani and Koufman. Alabama answered on the power play less than two minutes later, as the Icepack continued to struggle with penalties. Despite the abundance of penalties called against the Icepack, Jack Ammons scored N.C. State’s second shorthanded goal of the night, 15:07 into the third period. The Frozen Tide was assessed its second game misconduct of the night late in the period, allowing Zach Herman to score on the power play with six seconds remaining in the game, capping off an 8-5 win for N.C. State.
Following Friday night’s offensive display, the Icepack began looking ahead to its next matchup with the Frozen Tide less than 24 hours later, with a series sweep on its mind.

Saturday’s game began with Jake Gifford getting the Icepack on the board early in the first period, assisted by Herman and Lincoln Burns. Alabama was assessed a minor penalty for slashing roughly two minutes later, but N.C. State couldn’t find a way to extend its lead. The Frozen Tide scored later in the period to tie the game, and after multiple penalties were called against the Icepack, Alabama took its first lead of the weekend 19:52 into the period on the power play. Penalties continued to be a problem for the Icepack, leading to a 1-2 deficit entering the first intermission.

In another penalty-filled period for both teams, the Frozen Tide extended its lead on the power play early in the second period. Alabama scored again less than a minute later to make it a three-goal game, giving the Frozen Tide all of the momentum. Noah Fitzsimons attempted to give the Icepack some life midway through the period, scoring a goal assisted by Reece Johnson and Herman. Alabama found the back of the net minutes later, regaining its three-goal lead. Fitzsimons scored his second goal of the night 15:38 into the period, assisted by AJ Scarafoni and Johnson. The period closed with matching minor penalties assessed to the Icepack and the Frozen Tide, sending the game into the third period with N.C. State trailing 3-5.

The third period saw the Icepack trying everything it could to make up ground. Ammons gave N.C. State momentum with a goal midway through the period, assisted by Napieralski. Shook tied the game for the Icepack 5:48 into the third period, assisted by Prazma and Napieralski. The Frozen Tide regained its lead later in the period before sealing the game with another goal at 18:14. No penalties were assessed to either team during the period, marking the first time all weekend that a period went penalty-free. However, Alabama came away with the victory to split the weekend series, handing the Icepack a 5-7 loss.

Prazma recorded a hat trick during Friday’s game before adding an assist on Saturday, finishing the weekend series with four points in two games. Fitzsimons added three goals during the series, while Ammons and Koufman each contributed two goals of their own. N.C. State goaltender Pieter Bartelse got the start Friday night, stopping 23 of 28 shots and earning the win. Dillon Christy stopped 15 of 22 shots during his start in net on Saturday.

The Icepack return to Lane Arena this Thursday night at 9:00pm to start a two-game homestand against Cincinnati, with a 8:30pm scheduled puck drop Friday night, as the Icepack join forces with ZTA and the Raleigh Testicular Cancer Foundation to raise awareness for cancer. title: Skating down the frozen tide
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Alex Manuel/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. -   The Icepack prepare for a weekend series in Pelham, Ala., against the Frozen Tide, with games scheduled for Friday night and Saturday afternoon.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. -   The Icepack prepare for a weekend series in Pelham, Ala., against the Frozen Tide, with games scheduled for Friday night and Saturday afternoon.

N.C. State returns from an off-week, having last played on Oct. 24 in a winning effort against the University of North Carolina Tar Heels. The Icepack look to continue its recent momentum, posting a 6-1-1 record over its last eight games. The team has overcome a rough start to the season, finding consistency on both offense and defense while receiving reliable goaltending.

The Icepack and the Frozen Tide have already faced off this season, with Alabama coming out on top in overtime to advance to the championship round of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament. Alabama enters the weekend with a 9-4 record, good for second place in the SECHL. Icepack captain Zach Herman looks forward to the challenge ahead and emphasized the importance of the small details that lead to victory.

“I think we played a good game last time we played them,” Herman said. “It’s just the small details down the stretch that they did well and we didn’t do, which caused the result. We’re 15 games in. We know what to do, it just comes down to execution.”

The weekend series will also be a battle between two high-powered offenses, as both teams have found success putting the puck in the back of the net. Herman believes that the younger players on the team have been great for the Icepack’s offense, helping build chemistry and establish better relationships with the new additions.

“We’ve all gotten closer as the season has progressed,” Herman said. “You can see that translate onto the ice, we’re starting to click. It starts with the older guys setting the example, but giving the freedom to let the younger guys get after it. Whoever’s going is going.”

N.C. State’s defense will have to be up to the task against a Frozen Tide offense that has scored 66 goals in 13 games. The Icepack will look to stick to its defensive strategies that have proved fruitful during this recent stretch of success, and that starts with quickening the pace of the game.

“I think we’ve found a lot of success recently from our defensemen getting the puck up quickly,” Herman said. “The forwards have to get open and the defensemen have to get the puck to them quickly, and both units have been clicking to get the puck into the net.”

Friday’s game against Alabama will start at 9:50pm, while Saturday’s game features an earlier puck drop at 2:45pm. Streaming links for the games will be available via Alabama’s social media networks and BlackDog Hockey, additional links will be provided if they become available.

title: icepack split home-and-home series against unc
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Kaydee Gawlik/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. -  Over the course of a heated weekend against its rivals from right down I-40, the Icepack split the series with the University of North Carolina Tar Heels, dropping Friday night’s g...
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. -  Over the course of a heated weekend against its rivals from right down I-40, the Icepack split the series with the University of North Carolina Tar Heels, dropping Friday night’s game at Lane Arena before defeating UNC at the Orange County Sportsplex in Hillsborough.​

Friday’s game brought out the crowd and the energy at Lane Arena, as Icepack fans anticipated the next chapter in the storied rivalry. Mason Payne scored his first goal of the season for the Icepack, assisted by Daniel Prazma, to open the scoring. However, UNC seemed to control the pace of the game, hemming the Icepack into its own zone and forcing N.C. State goaltender Ethan Roberts to make some big saves throughout the period. A hooking minor assessed against the Icepack late in the period was successfully killed off, but this only seemed to further the Tar Heels’ momentum. Roberts stopped every shot he faced in the first period, sending the teams to the locker room for intermission with the Icepack leading 1-0.

The second period got off to a fast start, as UNC tied the game just 28 seconds in. From that point on, the aggression from both teams seemed to ramp up, as matching roughing penalties were assessed against the Icepack and the Tar Heels roughly a minute later, leading to four-on-four hockey. UNC scored again with more space on the ice to take the lead, but a Tar Heels player was assessed a cross checking penalty immediately after the goal, sending the Icepack to the power play. During the man advantage, another penalty was assessed against UNC for too many men on the ice, which gave N.C. State a five-on-three advantage, though the Icepack were unable to capitalize. Shortly after the penalty was killed off, the Tar Heels scored their third goal of the period. Adding to the penalty-filled period, UNC was assessed another hooking penalty late in the frame, allowing Holden Koufman to answer with a power play goal for the Icepack, assisted by Prazma and Andrew Throndson. The Icepack’s momentum was quickly quelled, however, as UNC scored again just 14 seconds later to reclaim a two-goal lead. The second period came to a close, with the Icepack searching for answers and trailing 2-4.

Icepack goaltender Pieter Bartelse was given the nod to start the third period, replacing Roberts. An early penalty against the Tar Heels led to another power play goal by Koufman, assisted by Prazma and Nick Shook. UNC once again answered quickly, scoring less than a minute later. Jack Ammons scored for the Icepack to make it a one-goal game 9:21 into the third period, assisted by Shook. UNC found itself on the penalty kill again shortly after Ammons’ goal but managed to kill off the penalty. The Tar Heels scored 13:22 into the third period, restoring its two-goal lead. The remainder of the game grew increasingly chippy, with multiple penalties assessed against both teams, and no more goals were scored. The Icepack suffered its first regulation defeat since Sept. 26, when it lost to Liberty.
The Icepack needed to put Friday’s loss behind it quickly, as the team knew it had another opportunity the very next day in Hillsborough against the Tar Heels.

Saturday’s contest saw N.C. State strike first once again following an early UNC penalty. Ethan Hoover scored his first goal as a member of the Icepack on the power play, assisted by Zach Herman and Reece Johnson. Fellow freshman Ethan Walters also tallied his first goal with the Icepack 6:19 into the first period, assisted by Ian Buckley. Three penalties were called midway through the first period, two of which went against the Icepack, allowing UNC to score on the power play to cut its deficit in half. Although the first period was riddled with penalties, the Icepack seemed to control the pace of the game. N.C. State ended the first period with a 2-1 lead.

The second period was the calmest of the weekend, with only three penalties assessed and no goals scored. The Icepack’s defense came up big, as UNC had very little time to generate offense in its zone. N.C. State generated some quality shots on goal but couldn’t capitalize. Both coaching staffs must have been relieved that the penalties were less frequent in this period, giving each team’s penalty-kill unit a chance to breathe. The Icepack maintained its 2-1 advantage heading into the final intermission in Hillsborough.

Officials assessed the Icepack a minor penalty for elbowing just 25 seconds into the third period, but N.C. State successfully killed off the early infraction. Following another penalty against the Icepack, UNC tied the game 8:18 into the third period. This seemed to rattle the Icepack initially, as N.C. State was assessed yet another minor penalty, though the Icepack killed it off. The remainder of the period was a battle, with both teams doing everything it could to take the lead. The Icepack eventually found the game-winner courtesy of Prazma 16:36 into the third period, assisted by Shook and Erik Dahlin. The Icepack held on to win 3-2, with Bartelse delivering a tremendous pad save in the closing moments. Bartelse started Saturday’s game after playing the third period on Friday night.

Prazma finished the weekend with four points across two games, including Saturday’s game-winning goal. Roberts stopped 17 of 21 shots during his two periods of play on Friday, while Bartelse stopped 30 of 34 shots over four periods of play during the weekend.
N.C. State will have this week off before traveling to Alabama to face the Frozen Tide during the weekend of Nov. 6.

title: Icepack look ahead TO WEEKEND SERIES AGAINST RIVAL UNC
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Alex Manuel/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. - The rivalry between N.C. State and UNC needs no introduction. It’s no secret that the two teams don’t like each other, setting the stage for plenty of tension throughout the game. T...
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. - The rivalry between N.C. State and UNC needs no introduction. It’s no secret that the two teams don’t like each other, setting the stage for plenty of tension throughout the game. The Icepack won three of four matchups against the Tar Heels last season, including a 7-0 win in the Governor’s Cup game at the Lenovo Center.

The Tar Heels enter the series with a 6-6 record and plenty of rest. UNC hasn’t played since Oct. 11, when it defeated Northern Illinois University in overtime in its final game of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament. The Heels boast a productive offense, averaging 3.92 goals per game, just below the Icepack’s mark of four goals per game.

N.C. State enters the weekend with a 6-4-2 record, having won five of its last six games. The Icepack has found its groove on offense, with every line deployed by Head Coach Nagib Ward contributing to the teams’ production. On the blue line, N.C. State’s defensive core is beginning to come together. As the season has progressed, the Icepack have begun to limit defensive lapses and establish a consistent forecheck that opponents have struggled to handle.

Icepack senior Jake Gifford is no stranger to the rivalry or how much it means to each team. He and other team veterans spoke with first-year N.C. State players about the importance of the rivalry. “We talked about it in the locker room,” Gifford said. “There’s a lot of energy around it, and the crowd’s always big. UNC’s right down the street, so it’s definitely fun to play in.”

As both teams look forward to the series this weekend, each club will need to focus on the strategies that will lead to victory. N.C. State looks to carry over the aggressive forecheck it’s developed in recent games, which has helped the team maintain puck possession, create scoring opportunities, and limit chances for the opposition.
“We just have to stick to the systems,” Gifford said. “Grab every loose puck and play as a team.”

title: icepack sweep weekend series against west virginia
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Alex Manuel/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. - The Icepack swept its weekend series against the West Virginia Mountaineers with a 5-4 overtime win Friday night, and a 6-3 win Saturday to move to 6-4-2 on the season.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. - The Icepack swept its weekend series against the West Virginia Mountaineers with a 5-4 overtime win Friday night, and a 6-3 win Saturday to move to 6-4-2 on the season.

N.C. State has been working on getting off to better starts in its games, and Friday’s game showed its progress. The Icepack played with tremendous pace early, pressuring the Mountaineers with its forecheck and threatening the West Virginia goaltender with numerous shots. Lincoln Burns struck first for the Icepack 8:11 into the first period, assisted by Jake Gifford. The goal was a sign of things to come, as a little more than three minutes later, Gifford doubled the Icepack’s lead, assisted by Burns and Lucas Collins. The Icepack then headed to the power play, as a West Virginia player cross checked Gifford from behind right after the goal was scored. However, N.C. State couldn’t capitalize. The Mountaineers cut the lead to one later in the period, and a late penalty against the Icepack seemed to give West Virginia some momentum. Icepack goaltender Ethan Roberts held his ground, maintaining a 2-1 Icepack lead heading into the second period.

The second period began with an early penalty against the Icepack, though they were able to kill it off. This seemed to restore N.C. State’s confidence, as Noah Fitzsimons scored 7:34 into the second period, assisted by Reece Johnson and Andrew Throndson. Less than two minutes later, Burns tallied his second goal of the night, assisted by Zach Herman and Gifford, to give the Icepack a three-goal lead. Following a successful penalty kill later in the period, the Mountaineers scored to cut the deficit to two, sending both teams into the locker rooms with the Icepack leading 4-2.

West Virginia seemed to build on its strong finish to the second period, scoring early in the third period to make it a one-goal game. The Mountaineers took control of the game, as the Icepack found itself under constant pressure from a more aggressive West Virginia forecheck. N.C. State took a penalty halfway through the period, and even though they were able to kill it off, it only seemed to give the Mountaineers more momentum. West Virginia tied the game at four 12:14 into the third period, stunning the Lane Arena crowd. Both teams played out the rest of the period with no goals or penalties, sending the game into overtime tied 4-4.

N.C. State regrouped during the brief break before overtime and dominated most of the extra period. Icepack defenseman Andrew Throndson scored his first goal of the season 2:19 into overtime to win the game, assisted by Fitzsimons and Jack Ammons.

The Icepack maintained its composure and held on for the win against a tough Mountaineer team. Icepack freshman Lincoln Burns hopes the team’s resilience is a sign of things to come. “I’m glad the boys could pull it out,” Burns said. “We’re finding our game as a group, and hopefully it’ll carry over.”

Burns provided the Icepack with consistent offensive pressure throughout the game, totaling two goals and an assist. The freshman has seemed to find his rhythm when paired with Icepack senior Jake Gifford, who’s become a mentor for Burns: “He’s taken me under his wing,” Burns said. “I’ve known him for a while, he’s a great hockey player and it’s just been exciting to play on the same line with two great guys.”
Following its overtime win, the Icepack had little time to celebrate, as the team returned to Lane Arena less than 24 hours later for another matchup against the Mountaineers.

Saturday’s game featured a 9:37pm puck drop, though neither team played as if it were tired. The energy was high from the start, with Icepack forward Daniel Prazma opening the scoring 6:05 into the first period, assisted by Ethan Hoover and Mason Payne. A penalty against the Icepack minutes later allowed the Mountaineers to tie the game on the power play. Two penalties were called during the remainder of the period, one on each team. Both penalty kills were sharp, keeping the game tied at one heading into the first intermission.

Freshman AJ Scarafoni scored his first goal as a member of the Icepack 1:19 into the second period, assisted by Fitzsimons and Burns. The Mountaineers tied the game again halfway through the period, as the momentum continued to swing back and forth. A penalty against West Virginia less than two minutes after the tying goal gave the Icepack a man advantage. Although N.C. State was unable to capitalize on the power play itself, Aidan Raedy regained the Icepack’s lead seconds after the penalty expired, assisted by Jack Ammons. The Icepack dominated puck possession during the period, as West Virginia began to struggle against N.C. State’s relentless forecheck. The Mountaineers survived some late scoring chances from the Icepack, sending both teams into the third period with N.C. State leading 3-2.

The third period began with two penalties against the Icepack within a minute of each other, giving West Virginia a five-on-three advantage. N.C. State’s penalty kill did its job, preventing a goal, which seemed to drain the energy from the Mountaineers even more. Ammons scored minutes later, assisted by Ethan Walters and Payne. Following two Mountaineer penalties within five seconds of each other, Gifford scored on the five-on-three power play to give the Icepack a three-goal lead, assisted by Hoover and Johnson. West Virginia scored with less than two minutes remaining and pulled its goalie shortly afterward. An untimely line change allowed Johnson to score an empty-net goal for the Icepack, assisted by Holden Koufman. N.C. State won 6-3, capping off the weekend with a strong performance.

AJ Scarafoni has been a tremendous addition to the Icepack, providing N.C. State with reliable defense whenever he’s on the ice. Scarafoni scored his first goal of the season during Saturday’s win and hopes it’s only the beginning. “It felt great to get the first one,” Scarafoni said. “I’m hoping there’s many more after that, and getting the sweep was even better.”

The Icepack now looks ahead to its most anticipated stretch of games this season: a home-and-home series against its rivals from Chapel Hill, the Tar Heels of the University of North Carolina. Scarafoni looks forward to the challenge and hopes to make an impact during the series. “I’m really excited for the weekend ahead,” Scarafoni said. “I’m looking forward to putting my own spin on the rivalry.”

Roberts stopped 21 of 25 shots during Friday’s overtime win, while Bartelse stopped 27 of 30 shots Saturday night. Both Icepack goaltenders made key saves throughout the weekend. N.C. State is now 5-0-1 in its last six games.

title: icepack defeat farmingdale in final game of stephen russell memorial tournament
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Kaitlyn Alumbaugh/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. -  The Icepack defeated the Farmingdale Rams 4-2 in the consolation bracket of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament, marking N.C. State’s final game of the event.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. -  The Icepack defeated the Farmingdale Rams 4-2 in the consolation bracket of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament, marking N.C. State’s final game of the event.

N.C. State attempted to settle into the game the same way it has in every game of the tournament: establishing an aggressive forecheck to limit scoring chances for its opponent and create opportunities of its own. Early in the period, this seemed to be the case, and a power play gave the Icepack a chance to take the lead. However, after failing to score, the pace and control of the game seemed to even out, with Farmingdale beginning to open up the ice and threaten N.C. State goaltender Pieter Bartelse. Two Icepack penalties gave the Rams momentum as the period neared its end, though Bartelse stopped every shot he faced. The game was scoreless at the end of the first.

The Rams opened the scoring at 5:50 of the second period, building on a strong finish to the first. Seven seconds after N.C. State killed off a roughing penalty, Icepack sophomore Kyler Sun answered with his first goal of the season, assisted by Holden Koufman and Mason Payne. Jack Ammons gave the Icepack the lead later in the period, assisted by Koufman. Both teams then intensified their forechecks as the period grew more contentious, with big hits delivered by both sides. Bartelse remained sharp, sending the game into the second intermission with the Icepack leading 2-1.

The third period began with an early goal from Ammons, assisted by Sun, to extend the Icepack’s lead to two. Ammons’ goal appeared to frustrate Farmingdale, as a Rams player delivered a questionable cross check to the back of Icepack senior Jake Gifford while he was down on the ice. Officials penalized the Rams for the cross check, and a bench minor was also assessed, giving the Icepack a five-on-three advantage. However, they were unable to capitalize on the power play. A slashing penalty and a game misconduct assessed to Farmingdale later in the period gave the Icepack another opportunity with the man advantage, but they were stifled again. The Rams managed to cut the deficit to one less than 30 seconds after killing off the penalty. Icepack forward Daniel Prazma scored at 13:18 of the third period to restore the two-goal advantage, assisted by Ammons. Farmingdale failed to score on a late power play, and N.C. State sealed the win shortly afterward, defeating the Farmingdale Rams 4-2 to record its second win in three games of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament.

Ammons scored his team-leading 10th goal of the season, while Prazma tallied his seventh goal in the last four games. Bartelse made 25 saves on 27 shots in his first start since September 26 at Liberty.

Sun, who recorded his first points of the season, maintained a team-focused mindset when asked how it felt to get on the scoresheet. “It was exciting,” Sun said. “We really needed another win after the loss against Alabama. It gets us back on track, and we’re playing well. It feels like we’re back in the groove of things for further games.”

The Icepack now look ahead to this weekend’s series at Lane Arena against West Virginia. “They’re always a good challenge for us,” Sun said. “We went there last year and played very well, but it’s a new year and they have a new team. It’s important that we’re finally finding some secondary scoring after struggling with that earlier in the year, so I feel like we have a very good chance to be competitive with them.”

title: Icepack fall to alabama in overtime, move to consolation bracket of the stephen russell memorial tournament
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Julia Ortiz/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. - The Icepack were defeated by the Alabama Frozen Tide in overtime in the second round of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament, 3-4.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. - The Icepack were defeated by the Alabama Frozen Tide in overtime in the second round of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament, 3-4.

The first period opened at a pace similar to Friday night’s game, with the Icepack maintaining possession of the puck. However, aggressive forechecking from N.C. State prevented the Frozen Tide from creating many offensive-zone opportunities, while the Icepack struggled to establish an offensive rhythm of their own. An interference penalty against Alabama at 15:48 gave the Icepack a chance to build momentum, but the Frozen Tide capitalized on a breakaway opportunity to open the scoring while shorthanded. The period ended with Alabama being assessed a holding penalty in the final minute, sending the Icepack into the intermission on the power play but trailing 1-0.

After an early penalty was called against the Icepack to open the second period, N.C. State’s penalty kill stepped up to keep the deficit at one. The two teams then traded power plays in the ensuing minutes before Reece Johnson tied the game for the Icepack at 13:49 of the second period, assisted by Noah Fitzsimons and Holden Koufman. Alabama reclaimed the lead less than a minute later to make it 2-1. The Frozen Tide were then assessed a roughing penalty at 15:55, allowing Daniel Prazma to find the equalizer for N.C. State with assists from Nick Shook and Jack Ammons. With the score tied at two, the Frozen Tide headed into the intermission on the power play after the Icepack were called for interference at 18:07.

Alabama received a roughing penalty early in the third period, allowing Prazma to score his second power play goal of the night, assisted by Andrew Throndson. The Icepack killed off the first of two penalties assessed against them in the period, but a slashing penalty at 15:58 led to an Alabama goal 19 seconds later, tying the game once again. The Frozen Tide controlled possession of the puck for the remainder of the period, but they couldn’t find a winner in regulation. The Icepack found themselves heading to overtime for only the second time this season.

Overtime began with N.C. State generating a few scoring chances while in possession of the puck, but Alabama scored the game-winning goal just 1:15 into the extra period. The Icepack fell 3-4 to the Frozen Tide, meaning they’ll move to the consolation bracket of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament. Roberts stopped 51 of 55 shots, while Prazma scored two power play goals.

title: Icepack shutout mercyhurst in the first round of the stephen russell memorial tournament
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Alex Manuel/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. - The Icepack defeated the Mercyhurst Lakers 7-0 in the first round of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament Friday night at Lane Arena.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. - The Icepack defeated the Mercyhurst Lakers 7-0 in the first round of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament Friday night at Lane Arena.

N.C. State got off to a hot start, controlling possession and preventing Mercyhurst from settling into its game. Zach Herman opened the scoring 5:37 into the first period for the Icepack, assisted by Jake Gifford. N.C. State dominated board battles to generate turnovers and create more scoring opportunities, though the team was unable to capitalize on them. Mercyhurst began to find its footing during the final five minutes of the period, requiring Ethan Roberts to remain sharp in his first start back to help preserve the Icepack’s 1-0 lead heading into the second period.

Jack Ammons scored his eighth goal of the season early in the second period to make it 2-0, assisted by Daniel Prazma and Nick Shook. Lincoln Burns scored his first goal as a member of the Icepack at 8:45 of the second period, followed by another unassisted goal from Prazma less than a minute later. After Herman was called for hooking 12:00 into the second period, Noah Fitzsimons scored a shorthanded goal for the Icepack off an assist from Ethan Hoover. Reece Johnson continued the offensive onslaught for the Icepack roughly two minutes later, assisted by Herman and Andrew Throndson. The Icepack ended the second period on the power play following multiple penalties assessed against the Lakers. Although N.C. State couldn’t extend its lead further, the team headed into the third period with a commanding 6-0 advantage.

The third period opened with a tripping penalty called against N.C. State’s Shook as Mercyhurst looked for any way to build momentum. The Icepack penalty kill did its job and set the tone for the rest of the period. N.C. State controlled possession once again, punctuated by Gifford’s goal to extend the lead to seven, assisted by Burns and Jack Napieralski. Goaltender Ethan Roberts held strong the rest of the way, sealing a dominant 7-0 win over Mercyhurst.

Roberts recorded a shutout in his first game back since undergoing hip surgery and felt great about his and his team’s performance. “It felt great,” Roberts said. “Coming off of hip surgery, you feel less confident in your movements, but I was able to trust it tonight, and it felt awesome. The boys dominated tonight and made my job easy, and they knew the situation, which helped me out a lot.”

With the win, the Icepack advanced to the second round of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament, where they will face the Alabama Frozen Tide. “We have to stay positive,” Roberts said. “They know us, we know them. We know we’re a good team; now we just have to go out there and show it. I’ve got to keep the vibes high and continue to be a leader for the younger guys.”

paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. - The Icepack will play its first game of the Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament Friday night at 8pm against the Mercyhurst Lakers at Lane Arena.

The tournament, previously known as the “Fall Showcase,” was renamed in 2009 after the passing of beloved N.C. State goaltender Stephen Russell. Wake Competition Center will host the tournament in its entirety for the first time since 2017. In 2024, the tournament was held at both Wake Competition Center and the Orange County Sports Complex in Hillsborough, N.C.

Icepack defenseman Andrew Throndson views the tournament as both an honor and an opportunity for N.C. State to prove themselves. “It means a lot,” Throndson said. “We had the tournament two years ago and didn’t play the way we wanted to play, but it’s a new year, with a new team and format. As the host team, we have to go in there like the team to beat and play with confidence.”

The Icepack have focused on building confidence and bouncing back from a rough start to the season. The Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament offers the Icepack the chance to pick up three wins in three days, but N.C. State will have to get through Friday first against a tough Lakers team.

Mercyhurst enters the tournament at 5-2 after traveling from Erie, Pennsylvania. The Lakers took the ice last Saturday, when they defeated Canisius 6-2 at home in the second game of a home-and-home series. Mercyhurst will be the fifth Division I opponent the Icepack has faced this season, as N.C. State still looks to record its first Division I win of the season.

Icepack forward Nick Shook looks forward to the challenge, emphasizing the importance of togetherness. “Playing together as a team is really important,” Shook said. “Just trying to gain some momentum from last weekend and carry it to this weekend is what we’re looking for.” N.C. State is coming off a 5-3 win against the High Point Purple last Friday, when the Icepack found an offensive rhythm and some much-needed momentum. The Icepack will have to build off that energy to get past Mercyhurst and progress in the tournament.

title: icepack wins 5-3 against high point on military appreciation night
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Alex Manuel/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. -    The Icepack snapped a five game losing streak with a 5-3 win over the High Point Panthers Friday night in honor of Military Appreciation Night at Lane Arena.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. -    The Icepack snapped a five game losing streak with a 5-3 win over the High Point Panthers Friday night in honor of Military Appreciation Night at Lane Arena.

N.C. State welcomed two of our nation’s finest for a ceremonial puck drop. Specialist Martinez and Sergeant Singleton, who both serve in the A-CO 1-505th 82nd Airborne Division out of Fort Bragg, were honored guests for the occasion.

The first period got off to a slow start for N.C. State, as High Point was able to create offensive pressure on the back of two penalties against the home team. However, Icepack captain Zach Herman opened the scoring with 3:02 left in the first period, assisted by Jake Gifford. N.C. State goaltender Dillon Christy kept the score at 1-0 with some key saves to end the period.

Icepack forward Daniel Prazma netted his first goal of the season to extend the Icepack’s lead at 15:27 in the second period, assisted by Holden Koufman. The Panthers got on the board roughly three minutes later, making it a 2-1 game. Following High Point’s goal, the pace of the game began to pick up. Great chances were generated on both ends of the ice, with each goalie having to come up with key saves. N.C. State regained its two-goal lead, as Gifford scored during a mad scramble in front of the High Point net, assisted by Aidan Raedy and Herman. Prazma tallied his second goal of the night 34 seconds later at 3:39 of the second period, assisted by Koufman. The period came to a close with the momentum squarely in the Icepack’s favor and a 4-1 lead.

N.C. State found itself with a man advantage early in the third period. Although the Icepack couldn’t capitalize, Prazma completed the hat trick shortly after the conclusion of the power play, assisted by Noah Fitzsimons and Ethan Hoover. High Point finally answered back at 13:35 in the third period. The Panthers scored again with less than two minutes remaining in the game to make it a two-goal game, pulling their goaltender shortly after. It would turn out to be all for naught, as High Point was assessed a roughing penalty with 57.9 seconds left. The Icepack closed out the game on the power play to win 5-3.
Christy put forth a great showing in net during his second start of the season, while Prazma found the back of the net for the first time this season, recording a hat trick.

Prazma, who has been an offensive force for the Icepack with seven assists in five games, was thrilled to get on the board himself this season. “A lot of the other guys have been stepping up and scoring,” Prazma said. “It felt awesome to get some pucks in the net.” The forward also commented on how special it was to get a win on Military Appreciation Night. “I’m so proud to wear that jersey with the camo on it,” said Prazma. “Being able to show appreciation to those who serve our country was amazing.”
The Icepack move to 2-4-1 on the season, as they now look ahead to the Stephen Russell Tournament next weekend at Lane Arena. For ticket information, click here.

title: Icepack drops both games of home-and-home series to liberty
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Julia Ortiz/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. -- N.C. State found themselves on the wrong side of both games in the home-and-home series against the Liberty Flames, falling to 1-4-1 on the season.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. -- N.C. State found themselves on the wrong side of both games in the home-and-home series against the Liberty Flames, falling to 1-4-1 on the season.

Friday’s game between the Icepack and the Flames saw another fast-paced start. With both teams trying to gain control of the game early, Liberty would strike first in the opening minutes to take a 0-1 lead. The Flames were able to settle into an offensive rhythm and hem the Icepack in their own zone, cycling the puck around the blue line to try and create open looks while maintaining pressure. Liberty would strike again at 8:12 of the period to make it an 0-2 game. N.C. State responded by directing shots at the Flames’ net from any spot on the ice that they could, as the Icepack tried to build some momentum. The rest of the period would see Liberty maintain possession of the puck for most of the time, with Icepack goaltender Pieter Bartelse making crucial saves to keep the game within reach heading into the second period.

The second period began with an Icepack penalty less than two minutes in. Although N.C. State would kill off the penalty, sustained pressure by the Flames lead to another goal for Liberty 30 seconds after the penalty expired, making it an 0-3 game. Less than two minutes after Liberty extended their lead, Jack Ammons would strike for N.C. State’s first goal of the night, assisted by Jack Ray. N.C. State would have to withstand sustained pressure from the Flames once again, but were able to create more scoring chances for the rest of the period, although they were unable to cut more into the lead. An N.C. State penalty late in the period would require Bartelse to come up big once again to end the period, with the score remaining at 1-3.

The final period began at an evenly matched pace, as both teams generated scoring chances. Bartelse would continue his great night with some key saves. The Flames would once again settle into the period and maintain pressure on the Icepack. A Liberty penalty midway through the period would give N.C. State a chance to build momentum, though they were unable to capitalize. Shortly after killing the penalty, the Flames extended their lead to 1-4. Liberty would add another tally late in the period on the power play to make it 1-5, a score that would hold until the final horn.
Following Friday night’s loss, the Icepack would look to get back on track the very next day. The team traveled to LaHaye Ice Center in Lynchburg, Virginia for the second game of the series.

N.C. State was able to match Liberty’s pace early on in the game and found themselves on the board first courtesy of an unassisted goal from Aidan Raedy 11:12 into the first period. The Flames would answer back less than a minute later to tie the game 1-1 before adding another tally later in the period. Liberty seemed to establish a similar control over the game as they did on Friday, with Pieter Bartelse having to make some big saves to keep the deficit at one heading into the second period.

The second period saw Liberty strike first with a power play goal two minutes into the period, which was then answered by Icepack rookie Noah Fitzsimons, assisted by Ammons and Andrew Throndson to make it a 2-3 game. After the Flames were given a major penalty for cross-checking, N.C. State found their equalizer on the power play 5:04 into the second period, as Jake Gifford was able to take advantage of a defensive breakdown by Liberty in the middle of the ice, assisted by Throndson and Fitzsimons. The rest of the period saw the Flames retake control of the game as Liberty would regain the lead less than 30 seconds after the Icepack tied it, followed by another quick goal 22 seconds after their fourth, making the score 3-5. N.C. State surrendered two more goals later in the period as the Flames settled into their game and maintained possession of the puck throughout the remainder of the period. Heading into the third period, the score was 3-7.

Goaltender Dillon Christy took over the net for the Icepack to begin the third period, as Bartelse put forth his best effort over five periods of hockey in two nights. Ammons opened the third period scoring for N.C. State with his seventh goal in six games, assisted by Throndson and Fitzsimons. The pace remained feverish as the Icepack scrambled to find opportunities to score while the Flames attempted to extend their lead. The Flames ultimately scored their eighth and final goal of the night at 12:31 into the third period. The Icepack would go on the power play shortly after but were unable to capitalize. The final horn sounded at LaHaye Ice Center, with a 4-8 final score in favor of the Flames.
Ammons recorded his team-leading seventh goal of the season during the series, while Bartelse put forth a strong effort in back-to-back starts.

paragraphs: LAKE PLACID, N.Y. - Despite a ferocious comeback in the third period, the Icepack fell to Indiana University of Pennsylvania (IUP) in a high-scoring 6-7 loss.

IUP sustained the pressure and scored an early goal less than five minutes into the period, followed by another less than two minutes later. After IUP responded with a tally of their own to retake a four-goal lead, Erik Dahlin scored his first goal of the season courtesy of Jack Ammons and Prazma. With N.C. State outscoring the Crimson Hawks 2-1 in the second, the Icepack looked to carry their newfound momentum into the third period.

IUP struck first in the third period, extending their lead back to four. Rookie Noah Fitzsimons found his way through a crowded net-front to score his second career goal as a member of the Icepack, assisted by Reece Johnson and Erik Dahlin. N.C. State rallied behind their young winger, who added another score roughly five minutes later on the power play, off assists from Prazma and Payne.

Less than a minute later, the Icepack found their equalizer at 10:28 courtesy of Holden Koufman, shorthanded once again, capitalizing on a rebound chance from Prazma and Napieralski.

The game reached a fever pitch from this point on, as both teams scrambled to find a winner. A costly N.C. State penalty gave way to an IUP power play tally, giving the Crimson Hawks the lead late in the third period. State created multiple opportunities to tie the game but were unable to capitalize. summary: LAKE PLACID, N.Y. - The Icepack was shutout by the Utes, 0-4, in the opening game of the 2026 ACHA Fall Faceoff Invitational.
paragraphs: LAKE PLACID, N.Y. - The Icepack was shutout by the Utes, 0-4, in the opening game of the 2026 ACHA Fall Faceoff Invitational.

State continued to battle, with both managing to slow the game down. Neither team surrendered a goal for the rest of the period, sending the game into the first intermission with the score at 1-0.

The Icepack looked to build momentum at the beginning of the second period, but found themselves in another evenly matched 20-minute bout. The Icepack weren’t able to find an answer in the second, but also didn’t allow the Utes to extend their lead. 1-0 was the score at intermission once again, heading into the third period.

Even with the Icepack generating better scoring chances and picking the pace back up, Utah was able to pull away in the third period. An early tipped goal from the Utes gave the Icepack a spark of life to answer back, snuffed out by a series of matching penalties. In the final five -- including one in the last 0.01 of regulation -- Utah added two more goals to the scoresheet. The final horn would sound at Herb Brooks Arena with the Icepack falling to Utah 4-0.

N.C. State will look to bounce back in Lake Placid against Davenport, whom they will play today at 3:30 p.m. Live coverage of the game will be provided on both X and Threads, with a livestream of the game available on FloHockey.​

title: On the Road to Lake Placid
author: Sage Kimbro/Icepack Hockey, Image by Alex Manuel/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH N.C. - Following their season opening win against Virginia Tech Friday night, the Icepack now look ahead to the 2026 ACHA Fall Faceoff Invitational. During their three-night stay in Lake Pl...
paragraphs: RALEIGH N.C. - Following their season opening win against Virginia Tech Friday night, the Icepack now look ahead to the 2026 ACHA Fall Faceoff Invitational. During their three-night stay in Lake Placid, N.C. State will take the ice against University of Utah, Davenport University, and Indiana University of Pennsylvania (IUP).

The Invitational will open with the Icepack taking the ice against the Utah Utes Thursday night at 8:00pm in the 1980 Herb Brooks Arena: an arena rich with hockey history. Home to one of the most historic games in hockey, “The Miracle on Ice”, that saw the United States Olympic Team upset the Soviet Union 4-3 on their way to winning the gold medal. The arena was eventually renamed to Herb Brooks Arena to honor the late Head Coach of that United States team.

Utah will be the Icepack’s first Division I test of the season, with the Utes finishing 15-9 last season. N.C. State will look to carry over its momentum from the win Friday night, and will need to do so by maintaining control over the game for the full 60 minutes. “I was happy with the first and third periods,” said Head Coach Nagib Ward, when talking about his teams’ performance in Friday’s season opener. “I was happy with the first six minutes of the second period.” In order for N.C. State to have the best chance to start off their trip to Lake Placid with a win, Ward will be looking for a complete game from the Icepack.

Friday will pit N.C. State against Davenport: another Division I opponent, who ended last season with an 18-17-2 record. This game will be a true test of Ward’s emphasis on conditioning during practices: “[In practices] I try to incorporate drills with a sprinting component, and a cognitive decision component as well.” Both areas of Ward’s practices could prove imperative to victory in Friday’s game against Davenport.

The Icepack’s final game in Lake Placid will see the team go against IUP, possibly one of the toughest opponents for N.C. State all season. Last season, the Crimson Hawks dominated the CHMA, posting a 27-4 record. Their 4 losses came only in shootouts -- meaning throughout the entire 2025-2026 season, IUP did not lose a single game in regulation. The Icepack have a great opportunity to end their trip to Lake Placid by taking down a premier opponent before returning back to Raleigh.

All Icepack games in Lake Placid will be covered live on both X and Threads, with livestreams of the games broadcasted via FloHockey. Each game will also be reviewed in its entirety following the final horn.

title: icepack wins home opener, 4-2
author: Sage Kimbro and Kaydee Gawlik/Icepack Hockey, Images by Alex Manuel, Alexa Tretola,  Julia Ortiz, and Lily McCabe/Icepack Hockey
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. -   The N.C. State Icepack opened the season with a 4-2 win over the Virginia Tech Hokies, the team’s first win under new Head Coach Nagib Ward.
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. -   The N.C. State Icepack opened the season with a 4-2 win over the Virginia Tech Hokies, the team’s first win under new Head Coach Nagib Ward.

To mark the 25th Anniversary of the September 11th tragedy, players learned about the Man in the Red Bandana, and heard from retired Army Special Forces Colonel Mark Ray on the importance of unity, resilience and determination. Icepack Class of 2000 Alum and Raleigh Police Selective Enforcement Officer Mike Mollere was welcomed back to the ice for a ceremonial faceoff to further honor the continued work of first responders in the community.

Gian Khani found the back of the net 22 seconds into the first period, assisted by Jack Ammons and Daniel Prazma. Virginia Tech tied it up just 28 seconds later for an eventful first minute of play. Rookie Noah Fitzsimons scored in his Icepack debut late in the first, assisted by Prazma to gain an early lead. The first period saw two penalties per team during a competitive pace.

Ammons pocketed his first goal of the season midway through the second period, assisted by Jack Ray. The Hokies would score to make it a 3-2 game shortly after. From there, Virginia Tech seemed to take full control over the flow of the period. N.C. State Goaltender Pieter Bartelse remained sharp to alleviate the pressure from the Hokies.

At 8:05 remaining, Ammons cemented the lead with a backhand goal assisted by Prazma. Aside from a scuffle at 15:34 that would see 6 players in total thrown out of the game with misconducts, the Icepack controlled the third period pace well. The intensive practices that led up to Friday evening paid off in a successful 4-2 home opener at Lane Arena, with a near-sellout to match.

“A lot of credit to my linemates, Gian Khani and Daniel Prazma,” Ammons said. “[Prazma]’s awesome. He’s one of the best players here: he shows up and makes plays like that so it’s very easy to play next to him.”
The Icepack head to Lake Placid next week to compete in the 2026 ACHA Fall Faceoff Invitational, facing off against University of Utah, Davenport University and Indiana University of Pennsylvania.​

paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. –  204 days since their last home game at Wake Competition Center, the 2026-2027 N.C. State Icepack will take the ice for the season opener against the visiting Virginia Tech Hokies this Friday night.

The puck will drop at 8:45pm inside the newly renamed Lane Arena (formerly Invisalign Arena). The Icepack will play one game at home before journeying up to Lake Placid to compete in the 2026 ACHA Fall Faceoff Invitational. Anticipation is palpable for the dawn of a new era under Nagib Ward, who was named the program’s new Head Coach this offseason following the departure of Tim Healy.

“Obviously things kind of change when you get a new coach,” explained Senior Goaltender Pieter Bartelse. “The practices are definitely higher intensity, all the guys are smiling the entire time we’re at the rink, having fun with it, competing and working hard... the overall vibe is just really high right now.” The team is adapting well to the new systems implemented by Ward. Friday sees a tough Division II opponent in Virginia Tech, and will test the change of pace.

The Hokies, who went 16-10-2 in the 2025-2026 season, will look to play spoiler against the Icepack in Friday’s home opener. Bartelse looks forward to the challenge: “Anytime someone comes and plays here they’re looking to get the edge on us and prove themselves, but we’re going to do what we always do: put our heads down and go to work.” A practical response in light of a mentally and physically demanding ramp-up toward puck drop.

title: NC State Icepack Announces Nagib Ward as New Head Coach
author: IcePack Media Staff
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. — After an intensive search, the NC State Icepack is excited to announce Nagib Ward as the program's next Head Coach. Ward, who has served as a part-time skills coach for the past two...
paragraphs: RALEIGH, N.C. — After an intensive search, the NC State Icepack is excited to announce Nagib Ward as the program's next Head Coach. Ward, who has served as a part-time skills coach for the past two seasons, brings elite technical and tactical acumen to the team.

"I am really excited about the opportunity and the chance to work with such a great group of guys," Ward said. "Coach Healy built a superior organization from the ground up, and we are going to leverage it to its fullest. Working with student-athletes who are excelling academically and are superior athletes will be really fun and rewarding."

Ward also emphasized his commitment to the broader NC State hockey community. "I’m looking forward to meeting and working with the alumni to continue building a program that this great university can be proud of. Our players have serious ambitions, and we look forward to putting exciting, quality hockey on the ice for our fans to see."

After nine years with the program, outgoing Coach Tim Healy expressed his full confidence in the hire. “Ward is the right coach at the right time in this program’s history," Healy said. "With the returning talent, a strong incoming class, and his vision and hockey IQ, the Icepack could not be in better hands.”

Originally from Evian-les-Bains, France, Ward grew up playing hockey in France and Switzerland. He later arrived in Minnesota for college hockey, playing at Rainy River Community College in International Falls. There, he was coached by the current University of Mary head coach, Dan Huntley, and helped lead the team to an NJCAA Final Four before moving on to Northern Michigan University. “I am extremely excited to see Nagib get an opportunity like this at NC State, a growing program in ACHA Division 1,” Huntley stated.

Following his collegiate career, Ward played professional and semi-professional hockey in France for the Flammes Bleues de Reims, Brûleurs de Loups of Grenoble, and the Pingouins de Morzine-Avoriaz. He eventually returned to the United States to pursue a career as a trained biochemist, serving as an executive at biotechnology companies, a path that led him to North Carolina, where he worked for Novozymes, Deinove SA, and his own company, AvantGarde Glycomics.

While in Raleigh, Ward founded Direct Impact Hockey, a training program that has successfully advanced players to the prep school, collegiate, and professional levels. He also coached various AAA teams within the Junior Hurricanes organization before joining NC State as a skills coach.

Icepack Captain Zach Herman is eager for the new leadership. “He’s an awesome person to be around," Herman stated. "He’s a very intelligent guy on and off the ice, and I’m looking forward to playing for him and learning from him. I think he is going to be incredible for this program and the people within it."

Former Carolina Hurricanes forward, Partrick Eaves, who will help support Ward, added, “Nagib Ward is a knowledgeable, developmental-focused coach.  NC State is lucky to have Nagib stand behind the bench.”

The Icepack extends its gratitude to Club President Jake Gifford for leading the coaching search. According to Coach Healy, Gifford's "work ethic and professionalism have ensured the Icepack will reach an even greater level of success in the seasons to come.”

Ward will officially assume Head Coaching duties on July 1st. As part of its continued growth, the Icepack will also add a General Manager and develop a Board of Directors comprising alumni, players, and other key program stakeholders. To facilitate the transition, Tim Healy will continue to serve as Acting General Manager.

title: Healy Steps Down as head Coach
author: IcePack Media Staff
summary: After nine years, including six as the Head Coach of NC State Hockey, Tim Healy will step down as his family returns to New Hampshire.  Healy oversaw tremendous growth during his tenure as an Assis...
paragraphs: After nine years, including six as the Head Coach of NC State Hockey, Tim Healy will step down as his family returns to New Hampshire.  Healy oversaw tremendous growth during his tenure as an Assistant Coach and Head Coach.  During his three years as an assistant, the Pack won two ACCHL titles, including the memorable undefeated season in the 2018-2019 season.  During his tenure as Head Coach, Healy amassed 116 wins and two ACCHL titles, but, more importantly, navigated NC State's rise to an ACHA D1 program and helped guide the team to memorable events like Frozen-Finley in 2023, where the Pack played in front of 26,000 fans.

In his own words, Healy stated; “Coaching NC State Hockey for the past nine years—including the last six as Head Coach—has been an honor like no other. Together, we have moved this program forward in ways I never could have imagined. We were able to do this through the support of a fiercely determined group of people, from our players and staff to our alumni and fans.

While this has been the hockey journey of a lifetime, I have made the difficult decision to step down from my Head Coaching role to pursue an outstanding career opportunity in secondary education outside of North Carolina. However, I will remain involved, continuing to work with NC State on our off-ice initiatives during this transition.

There are so many people who made this experience unforgettable. Thank you to every player who laced up their skates over the last nine years, and to my coaches and staff—Eric Mura, Alex Rossetto, and Jess Tart—who have been by my side this entire time. A special thank you to Mike Gazzillo for originally bringing me into NC State Hockey.

I also want to thank BJ Attarian and his crew at PackTV, as well as the leaders of our off-ice creative team over the years: Zak Salweah, Harrison Eaton, and Kaydee Gawlik. To Shane Willis and the Carolina Hurricanes, thank you for putting us on the biggest stages possible, from Frozen-Finley to the Hurricanes Alumni games.  Mario Ciardella from the Red and White Shop for believing in our brand and helping us reach our fans on a whole new level.

Thank you to our alumni—especially our founding group led by Richard Jordan—and to every single fan who tuned into a game, bought a ticket, or supported us in any way they could. Finally, thank you to my fellow coaches in the ACCHL, especially our commissioner, Mike Walley, and our local referees, led by Ricky Greene, for pushing me to become a better coach. Finally, the team at Wake Competition Center has given us the best home in the ACCHL.
This is not goodbye; we will be back to visit, and the Red and White from State will always be our family's college team. Go Pack!”

Healy will stay on and serve as General Manager during this period until his family relocates to New Hampshire, and will continue to advise and support Icepack's business operations throughout the full transition. Those interested in the position are asked to refrain from contacting the Icepack outside of the search process outlined here.
